newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea and Med crude markets plod along unchanged.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea and Med crude markets plod along unchanged.

text.p: North Sea crude markets were quiet and stable on Friday with few physical barrels left on offer in July and traders looking ahead to next month's loading programmes.

Mediterranean crude markets were paralysed by Turkey's tender for 300,000 tonnes of sour crude, due to be awarded on Monday, and a meeting between Iraq and the U.N. in Baghdad on Sunday to discuss a food distribution plan.
This week's high physical Brent values in Europe held steady after a July 24-26 loader passed between two majors on Thursday at 10 cents above August Brent, the same number as paid on Wednesday.
Differentials on other grades were similarly solid, with an end-month Forties traded at 40 cents above dated Brent, the same as Tuesday's traded level.

Just two other July Forties cargoes were believed still on offer, one or two Statfjord vessel-loads, a Troll and perhaps some Draugen barrels, a trader said. Two Beryls were rumoured traded on Thursday but could not be confirmed.
"We are pretty much cleared out," he said. "There is a little bit of buying, but most people are already looking to August and we're seeing nothing spectacular on the differentials."
The solid numbers, which are hurting refinery profit margins, reflect the tightness of a market still suffering from the absence of Iraqi sour barrels.

Refinery operators enjoyed some relief on Friday after outright values on the IPE fell some 25 cents to below $18 on news Germany planned to sell oil reserves to ease its budget deficit. At 1145 GMT August Brent was trading at $17.96 a barrel.
Cash Brent was quiet and stable, though prompt short-term swaps eased in the aftermath of busy Brent cargo business in the previous two days and weeks further out pushed up slightly.

Next week (July 14-18) was quoted at 18 cents under September, four cents down, while July 28-01 traded at -25 cents, up two to three cents. But brokers made little of the change, saying very few players were participating in the paper market.
Spreads were stable, with Aug/Sept changing hands at -10 cents.

Sour crudes in the Med were drawing strength from the Turkish tender -- there was unconfirmed talk of Russian Urals trading three times on Thursday at between Dated Brent -62 and -65 cents a barrel -- but some dealers sounded a cautionary note.
"Everyone is stalling for the time being waiting for the outcome of the tender. If there is positive news from Baghdad then it could encourage them to cancel it," said a trader.
Finalisation of the food distribution plan would remove a key obstacle to the resumption of Iraqi exports of Kirkuk Blend, suspended since late May.
The delay has driven up the price of sour crudes and left some refiners, Turkey's Tupras included, searching for alternatives.

Other grades offered into the tender are thought to include Syrian Light at around Dated Brent -35 cents a barrel, some 20 cents firmer than the July Official Selling Price (OSP), and Iranian Heavy at higher than Dated Brent -$1.80 a barrel.
With traders becoming increasing pessimistic about a swift resumption of Kirkuk exports -- some are now talking about the second decade of August -- prices could go even higher.

"If by Monday or Tuesday there has been nothing firm out of Baghdad then you may see some people having to scramble for August barrels of sour crude," said a Med trader. -- S.Maguire, M.Thompson, London newsroom +44 171 542 8060
